$comment: Literal redactions for text that must never be written into this repository, and
that has no pattern to match it — a client's name and a participant's above all.
placeholders.json holds regexes on purpose, so a rule never has to spell out the
text it removes. That works for anything with a shape. It does not work for a name:
there is no expression that matches this client, or the people in their interviews,
and nothing else. So every literal lives here, in a gitignored file, and nowhere in
the repository. placeholders.json carried a handful of them once; they were removed,
and NOTHING identifying goes back in — not even a value already in the history.
This example file is committed. local-redactions.json is not, and it has two halves:
redactions  GENERATED, and overwritten on every run:
node buzz-agents/scripts/refresh-local-redactions.mjs \
--key ~/.buzz/.secrets/claire-<slug>-service-user.json \
--dataset research_<slug>
It reads participants.participant_name and conversations.document_name,
so the list derives from the data rather than from whoever last noticed a
leak. Re-run after ingesting new transcripts: the guard only covers names
it has seen.
manual      HAND-WRITTEN, and carried through untouched by that script. For a subject
no dataset contains and nothing can re-derive:
- the client slug, and every spelling of it people actually type
- an operator's own name, given and full
- a retired credential or key-id fragment
- a participant identifier token that is not itself a name
Order matters: entries apply in sequence, so put the longest variant
first. "Ada Lovelace" before "Ada", or the surname survives as a suffix
on the replacement.
Losing this file loses the manual half for good. Nothing regenerates it.
find    the exact string. Matched on word boundaries where they apply, so a short
name does not rewrite the middle of an unrelated word. Under 3 characters
is refused as too collision-prone to be safe.
replace what appears instead.
label   what gets REPORTED when this matches. Never `find` — a leak warning that
prints the name it caught is the same exposure with extra steps.
